assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential account of how technology, trade exposure and task change reshape labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor's task framework and Dorn and Hanson's evidence on occupational and trade-shock adjustment form a coherent, influential core.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been extensively applied across labour, trade and regional research over a long period.
uncertainties: The listed contribution combines related but distinguishable mechanisms, making the most precise prize formulation important.
Attribution must distinguish central contributors from the wider literature on inequality and trade.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run evidence on income, wealth and offshore wealth has fundamentally changed the measurement and public understanding of inequality.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez established central distributional series and analysis, while Zucman made a major contribution on hidden and offshore wealth.
assessment.maturity: The research programme is mature, internationally influential and supported by a durable data-building enterprise.
uncertainties: Wealth and offshore-asset estimates necessarily depend on incomplete records and modelling assumptions.
The evidence is stronger on measurement and distribution than on any single causal account of inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the empirical study of intergenerational mobility and placed neighbourhood and institutional differences at the centre of the field.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked-data research programme and its measurement innovations.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a substantial body of replicated and extended work and has clear long-run policy relevance.
uncertainties: Interpretation of geographic mobility gradients as causal effects remains sensitive to residential sorting and design choices.
The candidate grouping leaves out other important contributors to mobility research.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of management practices made organisational capital a credible explanation for large productivity differences across firms and countries.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen supplied the formative measurement and empirical agenda; Sadun is a major contributor to its development and application.
assessment.maturity: The work has accumulated evidence across settings and linked firms' internal organisation to productivity, innovation and growth.
uncertainties: Survey-based management measures and causal interpretation remain subjects of methodological debate.
The field has a broad set of contributors beyond the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and organisational capabilities offers a deep alternative framework for understanding innovation, firm change and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is an indispensable architect of this contribution and the sole credited candidate.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have had enduring influence over several decades in organisational and innovation economics.
uncertainties: The central intellectual programme was developed with important collaborators not included in this candidate.
Its empirical implications are less sharply unified than those of some higher-ranked candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory and measurement of adverse selection in insurance materially improved understanding of market design, coverage and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie have each made central contributions connecting selection theory to empirical insurance markets.
assessment.maturity: A large subsequent literature has tested and extended the framework in health, credit and other insurance contexts.
uncertainties: Adverse selection is only one of several major frictions governing insurance-market outcomes.
The appropriate relative credit among a wider theoretical and empirical literature is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The political-economy analysis of institutions, state capacity and fiscal policy has supplied influential explanations for persistent development and governance differences.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are leading and complementary contributors to the modern institutional political-economy programme.
assessment.maturity: The theories and empirical applications have been developed and tested over decades.
uncertainties: Institutional variables are difficult to identify causally and often operate jointly with historical and social factors.
The broad programme includes many foundational contributors outside the listed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave rigorous economic expression to exhaustible resources, natural capital and the intergenerational value of biodiversity.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are both central to the theoretical foundations connecting environmental assets, development and welfare.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has long influenced environmental economics and is increasingly salient for policy and national accounting.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and inclusive wealth entails substantial conceptual and empirical uncertainty.
Translation from theoretical measures to practical policy remains incomplete.
